glossary.display: A screen. Never 'monitor' or 'screen' on its own, except in 'monitor speakers'.
glossary.your monitor speakers: The speakers or headphones the user plugged into a display. The app's central concept. Shortened to 'monitor speakers' in tight spots.
glossary.fix: The action: switching a display off and on to restore its sound. Never 'repair', 'cycle' or 'relink' in the interface.
glossary.no sound: The problem state. Never 'stuck' in the interface.
glossary.sound output: macOS's chosen output device, as named in System Settings > Sound.
glossary.LoudStation: The app's name. Never translated; always passed in as an argument.

comments.accessibility.status: VoiceOver label for the menu bar icon. %1$@ is the app name, %2$@ the headline.
comments.cli.app.not_found: %@ is the app bundle name; followed by a list of folders.
comments.cli.error.needs_value: %@ is an option such as '--hold'; keep it as is.
comments.cli.error.one_command: %1$@ and %2$@ are command names; keep them as is.
comments.cli.error.prefix: %1$@ is the command name, %2$@ the error message.
comments.cli.error.range: %1$@ option, %2$@ and %3$@ the allowed range, %4$@ what the user typed.
comments.cli.error.root: %@ is the command name. Shown when the command is run with sudo.
comments.cli.error.see_help: %@ is the command name. Keep '--help' as is.
comments.cli.list.on_display: Tag in the terminal. %@ is a numeric display ID.
comments.cli.status.couldnt_check: Status column in the terminal. Keep short.
comments.cli.status.hint_fix: %@ is the command name, which must stay as is.
comments.cli.status.hint_other: %1$@ is the command name, %2$@ a device ID; keep the command exactly as is.
comments.cli.status.no_sound: Status column in the terminal. Keep short.
comments.cli.status.sound_output: Tag after a display in the terminal.
comments.cli.status.working: Status column in the terminal. Keep short.
comments.confirm.cancel: Use the standard macOS Cancel wording.
comments.confirm.title: Alert title. %@ is a display name.
comments.display.connection_generic: Connection type when it is neither HDMI nor DisplayPort.
comments.display.fallback: Used when a display's name is unknown.
comments.display.with_connection: Disambiguates two displays with the same name. %1$@ display name, %2$@ connection such as 'HDMI' or 'DisplayPort'.
comments.display.with_connection_number: As above, plus a position number when name and connection are both the same.
comments.headline.all_working: Menu bar tooltip and first menu line when every display's sound works.
comments.headline.checking: Grey state while the first check runs.
comments.headline.couldnt_check: Grey state when a check could not run.
comments.headline.fixing: Blue state. %@ is a display name.
comments.headline.none: Grey state when no connected display can play sound.
comments.headline.others_silent: Orange state. Count of other displays without sound.
comments.headline.speakers_on: Second menu line under the red headline. %@ is a display name such as 'DELL U2518D (HDMI)'.
comments.headline.speakers_silent: Red state: the display with the user's monitor speakers has no sound.
comments.menu.check_every: Submenu title for the check interval.
comments.menu.check_updates: Menu item: asks GitHub now whether a newer version exists, then shows the answer in an alert, hence the ellipsis. Use the wording macOS apps use in your language.
comments.menu.check_updates_automatically: Checkable menu item: check for a newer version once a day.
comments.menu.fix_summary: Disabled line. %2$@ is a relative date and time.
comments.menu.follow_sound_output: Checkable menu item: the monitor speakers are whichever display is macOS's sound output.
comments.menu.interval.events_only: Interval choice: no timer, only check when displays change or the Mac wakes.
comments.menu.interval.minute: Interval choice. Menu title case in English.
comments.menu.interval.seconds: Interval choice. Menu title case in English.
comments.menu.last_checked: Disabled line. %@ is a relative date and time.
comments.menu.open_at_login: Checkable menu item. Use the wording macOS uses in System Settings > General > Login Items for your language.
comments.menu.quit: Menu item. %@ is the app name. Use the wording macOS uses for Quit in your language.
comments.menu.quit_after_fix: Menu item shown instead of Quit while a fix runs.
comments.menu.show_log: Menu item that opens the log file.
comments.menu.update_available: Menu item shown when a newer version exists; opens an alert explaining how to update. %1$@ is the app name, %2$@ the new version such as '0.3.1'.
comments.note.busy: Shown when Fix Now is chosen during a check.
comments.note.cant_autofix: Shown when automatic fixing is impossible on this setup, for example the only screen, a mirrored display, or two identical monitors that cannot be told apart.
comments.note.collateral: %1$@ the display that was fixed, %2$@ the display or displays that lost sound as a result.
comments.note.confirming: Shown while LoudStation waits a few seconds and checks the display again before an automatic fix, so it never acts on a momentary glitch.
comments.note.gave_up: Shown after two automatic fixes of the same display failed in a row.
comments.note.output_switched: Shown in the menu after choosing Set This Display as Speaker Output, which also makes the display the Mac's sound output. %@ is a display name.
comments.note.paused: Shown when automatic fixing has stopped trying.
comments.note.quitting: Shown after Quit while a fix finishes.
comments.note.speakers_missing: The display the user marked as having their monitor speakers is not connected.
comments.note.stranded: A display that the app switched off has not come back on yet.
comments.note.too_soon: Shown when another fix was attempted under a minute ago.
comments.note.waiting_call: Shown when automatic fixing waits because a microphone is in use.
comments.note.waiting_full_screen: Shown when automatic fixing waits because something is full screen on that display.
comments.notify.fixed.body: %@ is a display name. Apps keep the audio device they opened, so one that was playing may stay silent until it is quit and reopened.
comments.notify.fixed.body_collateral: %1$@ the fixed display, %2$@ the display or displays that lost sound as a result. The last sentence explains that apps may need reopening.
comments.notify.fixed.title: Notification title after an automatic fix.
comments.notify.paused.title: Notification title.
comments.notify.still_silent.title: Notification title.
comments.notify.stranded.title: Notification title.
comments.notify.waiting.title: Notification title.
comments.outcome.cycle_failed: %@ is a display name. 'Show Log' must match menu.show_log.
comments.row.plain: A display row without tags. %1$@ display name, %2$@ status word.
comments.row.tag.sound_output: Short tag on the display row that is macOS's current sound output.
comments.row.tag.speakers: Short tag on the display row that has the user's monitor speakers.
comments.row.with_tags: A display row. %1$@ display name, %2$@ one or two tags joined as a list, %3$@ status word.
comments.status.checking: Status word for one display. Keep very short.
comments.status.couldnt_check: Status word for one display. Keep very short.
comments.status.fixing: Status word for one display. Keep very short.
comments.status.no_sound: Status word for one display. Keep very short.
comments.status.working: Status word for one display. Keep very short.
comments.submenu.checked: Disabled line. %@ is a relative date and time such as 'today at 14:20'.
comments.submenu.counts: Disabled line: how often this display lost sound and how often it was fixed.
comments.submenu.fix_now: Menu item that fixes the display immediately.
comments.submenu.fix_now_confirm: Same, but it asks for confirmation first, hence the ellipsis.
comments.submenu.hint_others: Disabled hint under Fix Now for a display without the user's monitor speakers.
comments.submenu.speakers_here: Checkable menu item in a display's submenu: tells LoudStation that the user's monitor speakers are plugged into this display, and makes it the Mac's sound output, so this is the display it watches and fixes automatically. Menu title case in English.
comments.update.available.body_homebrew: Alert body. %1$@ the version in use, %2$@ the app name, %3$@ a Terminal command, which must stay on its own line after a blank line, exactly as given.
comments.update.available.body_source: Alert body for a copy built from source. %1$@ the version in use, %2$@ the app name, %3$@ the command 'make install'. 'Release notes' refers to the update.button.release_notes button.
comments.update.available.title: Alert title. %1$@ the app name, %2$@ the new version.
comments.update.button.copy: Alert button: copies the Terminal command to the clipboard.
comments.update.button.ok: Alert button. Use the standard macOS OK wording.
comments.update.button.release_notes: Alert button: opens the new version's page on GitHub.
comments.update.current.body: Alert body. %@ the version in use.
comments.update.current.title: Alert title after Check for Updates finds nothing newer. %@ is the app name.
comments.update.failed.body: Alert body when the update check could not reach GitHub.
comments.update.failed.title: Alert title.
comments.welcome.body: First-launch alert body: three short paragraphs separated by blank lines. Colours must match the menu bar icon.
comments.welcome.title: First-launch alert title. %@ is the app name.

strings.confirm.title: Fix %@?

strings.notify.fixed.body_collateral: %1$@ was switched off and on for a few seconds. This stopped the sound on %2$@. If an app is still silent, quit and reopen it.

strings.welcome.body:
The icon shows whether your displays’ sound is working. Green: everything works. Orange: a display you don’t use for sound has gone silent. Red: your monitor speakers have gone silent.

To fix silent monitor speakers, the app switches their display off and on. That screen goes black for about 3 seconds and its windows may move for a moment. It never does this to your only screen, and waits until calls and full-screen video are over.

It opens at login. You can change that in its menu.
strings.welcome.title: %@ is in your menu bar
